insight.title: For Millions of Years, Trees Didn't Rot
insight.subtitle: When trees first evolved, nature forgot to invent the microbes needed to decompose them.
insight.notificationHook: Earth forgot how to rot wood

sections.text: During the Carboniferous period, trees evolved a tough substance called lignin to grow tall. But for fifty million years, absolutely no bacteria or fungi on Earth knew how to digest it.
Instead of rotting, dead trees just fell and piled up in massive, dry, indestructible heaps. The planet became a giant, highly flammable lumberyard with forests stacked dozens of trunks deep.
Eventually, these endless layers of un-decayed wood were crushed into the coal we burn today. Our entire modern industrial revolution was powered by a fifty-million-year evolutionary glitch.
Nature invented the tree but forgot to write the delete code.
